title: Book Three · Chapter 11: The Other Shop
story:
After school on Friday, Ronan finds Anna near the gate.

She is looking inside her bag. A girl stands beside her with a closed umbrella.

“Lost something?” Ronan asks.

“My money. No, here it is.”

Anna takes a small purse from a side pocket.

“We are going to the bookshop,” she says.

“For school books?”

“I want a book of maths questions.”

“More squares?”

“Maybe. I want to look first.”

Her friend points toward the street. “This way?”

“Yes,” Ronan says. “I am going that way too.”

They leave the gate together. Anna's friend wants a notebook with a hard cover. She takes one out of her bag and shows them a bent corner.

“This one can't stay straight.”

“It lives under your lunch,” Anna says.

“That may be the problem.”

At the crossing, they stop. Two women pass with shopping bags. Then a man pushes a cart across the road.

Ronan can see the bookshop beyond the next corner. He usually buys pencils from Mr Qiu, but he has time to look at books today.

Inside, Anna goes straight to a low shelf. Her friend walks to the notebooks near the counter.

Ronan stops beside some drawing books. On one cover, a cat has very long legs.

He looks at the legs, then at Anna.

“Someone else draws like me.”

She comes over and looks.

“Your fish needs a cat like that.”

Then she returns to her shelf. She takes down two books and opens them side by side.

Ronan looks at the first page. There are numbers and small shapes. Farther back, the page has only numbers.

“Do you know all of it?” he asks.

“No. That is why I want the book.”

“This one has answers.”

“At the back. I want to try the questions first.”

She goes back to the first questions. She reads one, then checks the next page.

“I can try the first question in this book.”

Ronan looks at the other book.

“What about that one?”

“I need help with too much of it. I want to use the book at home too.”

She closes that book carefully. She wants the simpler questions. She opens the first book again and checks the print. The numbers are small, but she can read them.

She checks both prices. One book costs more. She puts it back and takes the other to the counter.

Her friend is still choosing a notebook.

“Blue or green?” she asks.

“Which cover is harder?” Anna says.

The girl presses each one. “The blue.”

“Then that one.”

They pay and go outside. Anna puts the new book deep inside her bag. Her friend carries the blue notebook in her hand.

At the corner, their ways part. The girls need the road to the left. Ronan needs West Lane.

“See you on Monday,” Anna says.

“Enjoy the squares.”

“Enjoy the cat.”

“I left it in the shop.”

“Good. It can't eat your fish there.”

Ronan laughs and crosses when the road is clear.

Near the green door, Mr Qiu is putting loose pencils into a box. Ronan buys one. He tests its point on a scrap of paper.

The first thing he draws is a cat with four very short legs.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

purse＝小钱包；side by side＝并排地；price＝价格；scrap of paper＝一小片废纸。

## 理解问题

1. Anna为什么想买一本尚不能全部做出来的数学题书？
2. Anna和朋友买完东西后是否继续陪Ronan回家？Ronan最后在哪里买了铅笔？

## 读句子

**She takes down two books and opens them side by side.**

拆开看：She / takes down two books / and opens them / side by side.

她／取下两本书／把它们打开／并排放着。
